{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{about|the mathematician|the author and philanthropist|Jessica Seinfeld}}
'''Jessica Katherine Sklar''' (born 1973){{r|born}} is a mathematician interested in [[abstract algebra]], [[recreational mathematics]], [[mathematics and art]], and mathematics and popular culture. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Pacific Lutheran University]], and former head of the mathematics department at Pacific Lutheran.{{r|cv}}

==Education and career==
As a high school student, Sklar studied poetry at the [[Interlochen Center for the Arts|Interlochen Arts Academy]]. She did her undergraduate studies at [[Swarthmore College]], where her mother Elizabeth S. Sklar had earned a degree in English (later becoming an English professor at Wayne State University) and her father [[Lawrence Sklar]] had taught philosophy. Jessica completed a double major in English and mathematics in 1995.{{r|cv|1plus1}}

Next, Sklar moved to the [[University of Oregon]] for graduate study in mathematics, earning a master's degree in 1997 and completing her Ph.D. there in 2001.{{r|profile}} Her dissertation, ''Binomial Rings and Algebras'', was supervised by Frank Wylie Anderson.{{r|mgp}}

She has been a faculty member in the mathematics department at Pacific Lutheran since 2001.{{r|cv}}

Combining her interests in mathematics and art she is one of 24 mathematicians and artists who make up the [[Mathemalchemy]] Team.<ref>[https://mathemalchemy.org/team-24-mathematicians-artists-of-mathemalchemy/ Mathemalchemy’s Team]</ref>{{r|beauty}}

==Selected publications==

*“‘Bok bok’: exploring the game of Chicken in film,” with Jennifer F. Nordstrom. In: [https://link.springer.com/referencework/10.1007/978-3-319-70658-0 ''Handbook of the Mathematics of the Arts and Sciences.''] Ed. Bharath Sriraman. Springer International Publishing, Cham, 2020.{{r|handbook}}
*“‘Elegance in design’: mathematics and the works of Ted Chiang.” In:  [https://link.springer.com/referencework/10.1007/978-3-319-70658-0 ''Handbook of the Mathematics of the Arts and Sciences.''] Ed. Bharath Sriraman. Springer International Publishing, Cham, 2020.{{r|handbook}}
*“Disciple” (poem). ''Journal of Humanistic Mathematics'' '''7'''(2) (July 2017), 418.
*[https://community.plu.edu/~sklarjk/fsaa/fsaa.html ''First-Semester Abstract Algebra: A Structural Approach.''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181114060414/https://community.plu.edu/~sklarjk/fsaa/fsaa.html |date=2018-11-14 }} GNU Free Documentation License, 2017.
*“A confused electrician uses Smith normal form,” with Tom Edgar. ''[[Mathematics Magazine]]'' '''89'''(1) (2016), 3–13.
*[https://mcfarlandbooks.com/product/mathematics-in-popular-culture/ ''Mathematics in Popular Culture: Essays on Appearances in Film, Literature, Games, Television and Other Media''.]{{r|mpc}} Jefferson, NC: McFarland & Co., 2012. Editor, with Elizabeth S. Sklar.
*“The graph menagerie: abstract algebra and the Mad Veterinarian,” with G. Abrams. ''[[Mathematics Magazine]]'' '''83'''(3) (2010), 168–179.
*“Dials and levers and glyphs, oh my! Linear algebra solutions to computer game puzzles.”''[[Mathematics Magazine]]''  '''79'''(5) (2006), 360–367.
*"Binomial rings.” ''[[Communications in Algebra]]'' '''32'''(4) (2004), 1385–1399. 
*“Binomial algebras.” ''[[Communications in Algebra]]'' '''30'''(4) (2002), 1961–1978.

==Recognition==
Sklar was a winner of the [[Carl B. Allendoerfer Award]] of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] in 2011 for her paper with [[Gene Abrams]], ''The Graph Menagerie: Abstract Algebra and the Mad Veterinarian''.{{r|allendoerfer}}
The paper provides a general solution to a class of [[lattice reduction]] puzzles exemplified by the following one:{{r|1plus1}}
{{blockquote|"Suppose a mad veterinarian creates a transmogrifier that can convert one cat into two dogs and five mice, or one dog into three cats and three mice, or a mouse into a cat and a dog. It can also do each of these operations in reverse. Can it, through any sequence of operations, convert two cats into a pack of dogs? How about one cat?"}}

She was the July 2012 Author of the Month at Ada's Technical Books in [[Seattle]], Washgington.
